analysis:
The PR makes three small test-only edits. It adds a `.boundedBufferCache(gib: 4)` trait to the suite in GLM5NextTensorParallelSpeculationRowsTests.swift (line 15). It adds the same trait to `sublayerCensus` and `projectionRowCensus` in GLM5NextTensorParallelWindowCensusTests.swift (lines 173 and 257). It adds the bare `.boundedBufferCache` trait to the suite in Gemma4StagePagedSyntheticTests.swift (line 21). The trait is defined elsewhere and was not supplied. Presumably it caps the MLX buffer cache during tests to limit GPU/RAM growth.

No production code changed. No coordinator-to-provider wire contract, attestation, App Attest authorization, key handling, prefix-cache (T-041) or fan-helper code changed. The tests use synthetic, deterministically seeded weights and prompts. They hold no real consumer data (A-001), keys (A-002, A-003), tokens or model weights (A-004). The GLM row test and census tests are opt-in via the `GLM53_ROW_INVARIANCE` and `GLM53_WINDOW_CENSUS` environment variables.

I see no new attack surface. The only gap in the evidence is the unseen trait implementation. If it mutated process-wide MLX state and failed to restore it, that would affect test isolation only, not shipped provider behavior. No threat-model update is needed.
